panels.title: JetStream consumer backlog (pending) by durable
panels.description: nats_consumer_pending — undelivered messages per durable consumer. Baseline 0. The NATS-outage chaos (CHAOS.md case 1) spikes this, then it drains within seconds on recovery (at-least-once). Sustained >50 for 5m fires NatsConsumerBacklogWarning.

panels.title: Max consumer backlog (now)
panels.description: Worst current pending across all durables. Green <50, red ≥500 (alert thresholds).

panels.title: Service liveness (up)
panels.description: up{job=...} per scraped service. 1 = scrape OK, 0 = down (ServiceDown alert at 0 for 2m). Truthful because prometheus scrapes the prod-stack container DNS (one instance/service).

panels.title: Rejected (unsigned/forged) events — rate
panels.description: rate(nats_rejected_events_total) — events that FAILED HMAC verification and were dropped fail-closed. Normally absent/zero; ANY increase fires NatsRejectedEvents (critical). The series only appears once a rejection has occurred (lazy counter registration).

options.content:
**NATS & outbox health.**

The v2 cross-service contract is JetStream events via a transactional outbox (booking/etc. write the row + the event in one DB tx; a relay publishes async).

- **Backlog (pending)** rising + sustained → a consumer is stuck (downstream delays). The NATS-outage chaos proves at-least-once: backlog drains within seconds of recovery.
- **Rejected events** → HMAC verify failed (fail-closed). Any non-zero is a security signal.

**Gap:** there is no per-topic publish-rate metric and no outbox-table-depth metric exported to Prometheus today; the outbox drain is verified via SQL in the chaos suite (`booking.outbox WHERE published_at IS NULL`). Exporting an `outbox_pending` gauge from the relay is a tracked follow-up.
